question: A man goes to Nagpur from Visakhapatnam at a speed of 20 km/hr and returns to Visakhapatnam at speed of 30 km/hr, through the same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same for both parts of the journey, the average speed can be found directly.

Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Here, the forward speed x = 20 km/hr and return speed y = 30 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 20 × 30) ÷ (20 + 30) = 1200 ÷ 50 = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Visakhapatnam to Nagpur (S₁) = 20 km/hr

Speed from Nagpur to Visakhapatnam (S₂) = 30 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the one-way distance between Visakhapatnam and Nagpur be D km.

⇒ Total distance for the entire journey = D + D = 2D km

⇒ Time taken for the forward journey (T₁) = D ÷ 20 hours

⇒ Time taken for the return journey (T₂) = D ÷ 30 hours

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 20) + (D ÷ 30)

⇒ Total Time = (3D + 2D) ÷ 60

⇒ Total Time = 5D ÷ 60 = D ÷ 12 hours

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (D ÷ 12)

⇒ Average Speed = 2D × (12 ÷ D) = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If a person travels non-equal distances D₁, D₂, D₃ at corresponding speeds S₁, S₂, S₃, then the Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂ + D₃) ÷ (T₁ + T₂ + T₃).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person travels three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the direct shortcut formula for average speed is (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

When two moving bodies are travelling in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When travelling in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).
